classroom.name: Discrete Mathematics

description: Discrete Mathematics provides the foundational language and tools of computer science. Topics include logic and proof techniques, sets, functions and relations, sequences and cardinality, induction and recursion, counting, graphs and trees. The course emphasizes clear mathematical reasoning, writing precise proofs, and connecting theory to real software: data structures, databases, cryptography, networks, compilers and AI.

philosophy.intro: We approach Discrete Mathematics as a language for precise thinking. Conceptual understanding comes before rote manipulation; clear definitions and well-structured arguments come before speed. Every week you meet an idea on the board and then make it run in Python.

points.d: Build intuition with concrete examples, then generalize and prove.
Each lecture is followed by a lab where the mathematics becomes code you test yourself.
Direct, contrapositive, contradiction and induction, chosen to fit the problem.
Use discrete structures to frame real problems in software, data, security and networks.
Challenge is expected. Feedback, collaboration and reflection turn confusion into insight.
Integrity in reasoning, attribution and reuse of ideas, including ideas produced with AI tools.

outcomes.text: Translate natural-language statements into propositional and predicate logic, and evaluate them with truth tables.
Apply rules of inference and construct direct, contrapositive and contradiction proofs.
Work fluently with sets, relations and functions, and use them to model data.
Reason about sequences, sums and the cardinality of infinite sets.
Prove properties with mathematical induction and analyze recursive definitions and algorithm growth.
Solve counting problems with the product and sum rules, permutations, combinations and the pigeonhole principle.
Model problems with graphs and trees, and apply isomorphism, connectivity and coloring.
Implement and test discrete-mathematics ideas in Python, and connect them to real software systems.

components.name: Midterm exam
components.note: In-class written exam. The official date is announced by the faculty.

components.name: Final
components.note: Final grade = 85% final exam + 15% semester project.

assessment.labsNote: Weekly labs are autograded for instant feedback. They are the practice ground for the exams and the project, and completion is tracked.

policies.d: Assignments submitted after the due date are penalized 10% per day, including weekends. Nothing is accepted more than five days late unless a documented medical or personal emergency is provided.
Cheating, plagiarism and submitting someone else's work as your own lead to disciplinary action, which can include a failing grade and university sanctions.

You may use AI assistants to explain concepts, generate practice problems and debug. You may not submit code or proofs you cannot explain line by line. In labs and project demos you may be asked to walk through your work.
Regular attendance is crucial. If you cannot attend, email the instructor in advance.
Laptops and phones are for course work only. Anything that distracts others is not allowed.
Official course communication is by email. Urgent announcements also go to the WhatsApp channel.
If you need an accommodation for a disability or any other reason, contact the instructor as early as possible.
